claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes - I have one child, Alex. He's 17 and still living at home with me. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 17 and living at home with you.

Since Alex is 17 (over 16), a key factor for eligibility is whether he is in approved education or training. 

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in college, sixth form, doing A-levels, or in approved training?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is - he's doing his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 17 and in approved education (doing A-levels), that's relevant to your eligibility.

Now I need to ask about your circumstances:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do - I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your responsibility for Alex:

**Are you the person primarily responsible for Alex - meaning either you live with him (which you've confirmed) or you're paying towards his upkeep such as food, clothes, or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely - he lives with me and I provide for him. I cover all his food, clothes, school expenses, everything he needs really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. A couple more questions:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he claiming any benefits in his own right** (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't - he's just focused on his studies at the moment. He doesn't work and he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Do you or your partner (if you have one) have an individual income over £60,000 per year?**

(This doesn't affect whether you can *get* Child Benefit, but it may mean you have to pay a tax charge on it, so it's important information for you to know.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into my income details right now - I'm mainly just trying to find out if I'm actually eligible to claim in the first place.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's absolutely fine - I have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me review your situation:

- You have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old
- Alex is living with you in the UK (Manchester)
- Alex is in approved education (doing A-levels)
- You are responsible for Alex and provide for all his needs
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex is not working 24+ hours per week or claiming benefits in his own right

Based on the rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. However, you'll normally still qualify if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training.

Since Alex is 17, still in approved education (A-levels), living with you, and you're responsible for him, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.
